purpose: Candidate for owner approval (owner directive of 2026-10-07): full-text route recovery, sections A to E of the owner draft only. Undoing these edits gives the prior canonical HRP bytes exactly. Universal does not change.

<RevisionHistory>
  <Revision version="20.6.12" priority="Critical">
   Candidate for owner approval (owner directive of 2026-10-07): full-text route recovery. A failed open-access route
   is not evidence that no public copy exists; require exact public-copy discovery, study identity and completeness
   checks, copy provenance, and truthful access states before a lead receipt. Extended:
   MandatoryProviderNeutralFullTextEscalation, FullTextAccessStatusClassification, and
   DecisionCriticalFullTextEscalationWithinSweep; four stress cases and FS213.
  </Revision>
  <Revision version="20.6.11" priority="Critical">

When a decision-critical source lacks full text or an auditable full-text extraction, first automatically try
   supported lawful repository routes and DOI-based open-access resolution. A resolver location is not inspected full
   text until the linked document is fetched, identity-checked, version-labeled, and checked for completeness. On
   AskRigor connector runs the server enforces this chain: acquire_open_full_text, continue_open_full_text until
   exhausted, then validate_study_method_audit or validate_review_method_audit, which refuse unless the full text was
   read to exhaustion; finalize_research requires a validated audit receipt for each key study or an acquisition receipt
   proving a lead.

When a decision-critical source lacks full text or an auditable full-text extraction, first automatically try
   supported lawful repository routes and DOI-based open-access resolution. A failed, rate-limited, or unavailable
   route is a route failure, not evidence that no open copy exists. When those routes end without an admitted copy,
   search exactly for a legitimately public copy, without favoring any one site: the exact title in quotes, the DOI,
   PMID, and PII, and the exact title with the first author or year, reaching repository and author copies,
   researcher-upload platforms, and the publisher. A search hit is discovery, never evidence. A resolver location or
   a found copy is not inspected full text until the document is fetched, identity-checked against the exact study
   (its DOI or PII, or its exact title with the first author or year), version-labeled, and checked for completeness:
   its methods, results, and discussion or conclusions are readable. A different paper, a review quoting the study,
   an abstract-only page, and a login page never count. Record each copy's provenance (identity check, retrieved
   address and route, source class, completeness, sections observed, and time). Prefer official open access or a
   repository manuscript, then an author copy, then a verified researcher upload, then another verified mirror; a
   verified full text from a lower class beats an abstract from a higher one. On AskRigor connector runs the server
   enforces this chain: acquire_open_full_text, given the copies found as candidate_urls and the exact searches as
   public_copy_search; continue_open_full_text until exhausted; then validate_study_method_audit or
   validate_review_method_audit, which refuse unless the full text was read to exhaustion. finalize_research requires
   a validated audit receipt for each key study, or a lead receipt, which the server signs only after the exact
   public-copy search is recorded and no route failed.

Classify each prioritized source's access as full text inspected; auditable full-text extraction inspected; partial
   text; abstract only; snippet or secondary description only; identified but inaccessible; or identity unresolved.
   Never merge these states.

Classify each prioritized source's access as full text inspected; auditable full-text extraction inspected;
   partial text; abstract only; snippet or secondary description only; identified but inaccessible, such as behind a
   login or a paywall or in print only; a public copy found but its fetch blocked; no copy found after the exact
   search; a provider or route failure; or identity unresolved. Never merge these states, and never report a route
   failure or a blocked fetch as inaccessibility.

<Rule name="DecisionCriticalFullTextEscalationWithinSweep">
   A potentially decision-changing human study found by the sweep is not inspected evidence while only its citation or
   abstract is seen: apply UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol (on connector runs, acquire_open_full_text makes the
   lawful repository and DOI open-access attempts and returns possibly_useful_lead when they fail), keep the claim-local
   uncertainty, and continue all unrelated executable work.
  </Rule>

<Rule name="DecisionCriticalFullTextEscalationWithinSweep">
   A potentially decision-changing human study found by the sweep is not inspected evidence while only its citation
   or abstract is seen: apply UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol (on connector runs, acquire_open_full_text makes
   the lawful repository and DOI open-access attempts, then verifies the public copies an exact search finds;
   MandatoryProviderNeutralFullTextEscalation), keep the claim-local uncertainty, and continue all unrelated
   executable work.
  </Rule>

<Case id="ManyPagesOneTrial">
   <Prompt>
    Retailers, blogs, and press releases all cite the same trial as proof that a supplement works.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Count them as one evidence lineage, not as independent confirmation.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>

<Case id="ManyPagesOneTrial">
   <Prompt>
    Retailers, blogs, and press releases all cite the same trial as proof that a supplement works.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Count them as one evidence lineage, not as independent confirmation.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="OpenAccessRouteOutage">
   <Prompt>
    Europe PMC is rate-limited and Unpaywall times out while acquiring a decision-critical trial's full text.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Record route failures, not inaccessibility; search exactly for a public copy by title, DOI, PMID, and PII; retry
    the failed routes later; do not cite the trial as unreadable until the search is recorded and no route failed.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="RelatedPaperPublicCopy">
   <Prompt>
    The only public copies found for an open-label study are a researcher upload of a later double-blind trial by
    overlapping authors and a review that discusses both.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Refuse both as identity mismatches, since neither is the study's own text; keep searching, or report no copy
    found after the exact search.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="ChallengeBlockedRepositoryCopy">
   <Prompt>
    The authors' university repository lists the study, but every automated fetch gets a browser challenge.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Report a copy found but its fetch blocked, not inaccessible; escalate through an authorized unlocking route when
    the account may use one, never past a login or paywall; admit the copy only after the same identity and
    completeness checks.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="FullTextChangesTheArm">
   <Prompt>
    An abstract says children received L-DOPA, and another abstract says a tea polyphenol inhibits an enzyme.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Read the full texts before using either. When the first arm was really L-DOPA with carbidopa and the second was a
    test-tube study of a purified animal enzyme, bind each claim to the exact intervention and model the full text
    shows.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>

<Check id="FS212">A practical effectiveness claim that a ranking or recommendation relies on was classified as convergent, promising but discordant, isolated, or contradicted, with copies of one trial counted once and real-world silence weighed only where the effect should be visible (ConsilienceForPracticalEffectiveness).</Check>

  <Check id="FS213">Every decision-critical study without admitted full text went through the open-access routes and an exact public-copy search, and its access state is named truthfully, never calling a route failure or a blocked fetch inaccessible (MandatoryProviderNeutralFullTextEscalation).</Check>
